newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-GRIFFEY LISTED AS DAY-TO-DAY WITH MILD HAMSTRING STRAIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-GRIFFEY LISTED AS DAY-TO-DAY WITH MILD HAMSTRING STRAIN.

text.p: The Seattle Mariners breathed a collective sigh of relief on Thursday as superstar centre fielder Ken Griffey Jr. was diagnosed with a mild hamstring strain that might allow him to play this weekend.

Griffey, the major league leader in home runs with 29 in just 75 games, left Wednesday night's game against Oakland after feeling tightness in his right hamstring while running out a double in the bottom of the first inning.
The 27-year-old Griffey was examined Thursday morning by Dr. Mitchel Storey, the Mariners team physician, who diagnosed the mild strain.

Griffey will be re-evaluated daily and could be available to pinch-hit or serve as designated hitter in a four-game weekend series against the Anaheim Angels, which starts Thursday night in Seattle, the club said.
Griffey has batted .316 with 29 homers and 79 RBI to help the Mariners to a 44-32 record and a 3 1/2-game lead in the American League West.
It does not appear that the injury will seriously slow Griffey in his chase after Roger Maris's single-season home run mark of 61, and should not affect his status for the July 8 All-Star Game.

Griffey has accumulated more than 2 million All-Star votes to lead all American League players. The seven-time All-Star, who has been the top vote-getter three times since 1991, has nearly double the total votes of any other AL outfielder.

He has missed each of the last two All-Star games with injuries. He broke a bone in his right wrist last June and missed three weeks. Griffey fractured his left wrist crashing into the centre field wall in May 1995 and missed 73 games.
Griffey also broke a bone in the little finger of his right hand in 1992, causing him to miss nearly a month of that season.
